byline.display: Prepared by the front office · Through May 5, 2040

lede.text: Build a deal and see what each side is worth. The decision is yours.

because.label: How to read it
because.value: Put the players you would send on one side and the ones you would receive on the other: drag them in from anywhere, search, or load an offer or a target from your inbox. Each player shows what his contract is worth, and below, the difference between the sides.

because.label: What it is not
because.value: A verdict. It reads contract value only: not fit, need, or what the other club wants.

basis.stamp: How the desk reads it: stated, not fitted

emptyDeal.display: Add players to each side to see what the deal is worth: drag them here, search, or load an offer or a target.

reading.text: Can't tell apart from an even deal: could be −11.2 wins to +3.8 wins (most likely −3.7 wins)

because.label: How it is read
because.value: The same reading the builder gives: what you'd receive less what you'd send, each player at his contract value. The sides are worked out from who each player plays for now, since the message doesn't store them. It isn't a verdict.

because.label: How the sides are added up
because.value: What comes in less what goes out, in wins over a replacement, each player's part named (a player going out enters reversed). players combined as independent; not a calibrated interval: around the sum of the most likely readings, each player's own distance combined as independent across 2 players (root sum of squares); an open season stays at its edges. Every player at his edge: −13.3 wins to 6.9 wins. The price of a win is shared by every player on both sides and is read as independent too, so the range is a reading, not a coverage claim.

wouldChange: A newer export, or a change to either side.
basis.stamp: Phase 6b (the owner's Payroll rule of 2026-09-24 extended to a trade; confirmed by the owner, 2026-09-24): a side's contract value and the difference between the sides are the sum of the players' most likely readings, each player's distance from his on each side combined as independent across players (root sum of squares), an open season (option, status, whether he stays) kept at its edges, added. Labelled "players combined as independent; not a calibrated interval"; the edge-to-edge sum is kept beside it and no player's own band is narrowed.

because.label: Contract value
because.value: What this contract is worth to any team that holds it: the wins he's projected to add, priced at what a win costs on this league's market, minus the salary still to be paid.

Labelled "players combined as independent; not a calibrated interval"; the edge-to-edge sum is kept beside it and no player's own band is narrowed.

because.label: What a message says
because.value: OOTP's messages name the player and the club but never the price, so reviewing one puts him on the side you'd receive and leaves what you give up to you.

weakest.text: Your weakest spots by expected wins: C (P 1012, 0.1 wins), 1B (P 1006, 0.2 wins), 2B (P 1001, 0.2 wins)

because.label: How fits are read
because.value: Expected wins this season (the part still to be played, most likely), from each player's projection. A match is a player who isn't his club's starter at a position yet is expected to add more wins than the other club's best there. Players whose production isn't established are left out. A lead to look into, not a verdict: the ranges behind these figures are wide.

because.label: What the wins are
because.value: Expected wins this season (the part still to be played, most likely), from Player Value's production. A match is a player who isn't his club's starter at a position yet is expected to add more wins than the other club's best there. Players whose production is not established are left out and never counted as zero.

because.label: What it is given
because.value: The deal on the builder with every figure Pennant worked out for it, and the run of the organization to look things up.

because.label: What it is not
because.value: Pennant's answer: the analysis is. It reads the deal and gives no answer of yes or no: the decision is yours.

because.label: How current
because.value: Pennant's copy of the league is from May 6, 2040. It couldn't find your OOTP save to compare dates with, so it can't tell whether the export is current: service time, control and the figures built on them are read as the export states them.
